**Preserve password protection before rendering stored content.**

For a password-protected issue, WordPress supplies the password form to `the_content`. This filter replaces that form with `renderIssue($post)`, which reads the stored newsletter directly. An anonymous visitor can therefore read the newsletter without its password. The `isIssue()` and `is_admin()` checks do not enforce password protection. ([developer.wordpress.org](https://developer.wordpress.org/reference/functions/get_the_content/?utm_source=openai))

Return `$content` when `post_password_required($post)` is true. Add a regression check for a visitor without the password cookie.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-    if (!isIssue($post) || is_admin()) {
+    if (!isIssue($post) || is_admin() || post_password_required($post)) {
         return $content;
     }
```

**Compose content before WordPress runs shortcode processing.**

At priority `20`, this filter discards the output of `do_shortcode`, which runs at priority `11`. It then renders the stored blocks again. A Shortcode block inside any accepted section will display its literal shortcode instead of its output. The Shortcode block renderer itself only applies `wpautop`; it does not execute the shortcode. Move composition before the standard block and shortcode filters, while preserving the password and email guards. Avoid applying the entire `the_content` filter recursively.

**Pass the `$escape` argument to the CSV functions.**

The plugin requires PHP 8.2 or later. From PHP 8.4, `str_getcsv()` and `fputcsv()` emit a deprecation notice when the call omits `$escape`. This keeps RFC 4180 behavior on all supported versions.

<details>

+    fputcsv($out, ['email', 'name', 'status', 'joined'], escape: '');

**Guard `sendCampaign` against concurrent requests.**

`sendCampaign` checks the delivery state with `deliveryStatus()` at line 365. It writes `DELIVERY_META` only at line 395, after `save_email()` at line 388. Two overlapping requests can both read `not_sent`. Each request then queues its own email, so subscribers can receive the same newsletter twice. Overlap can happen with a double click or with two staff members. Both requests reach this code through `rest.php:94`.

Take an atomic lock before the status check. `add_option()` fails when the key already exists, so only one request acquires the lock. Release the lock in a `finally` block. The stored timestamp lets a stale lock from a crashed request expire. Delete the stale lock and acquire it again with `add_option()`, rather than overwriting it with `update_option()`. This keeps the takeover atomic.

```php
$lock = 'omni_platform_newsletter_lock_' . $post->ID;
if (!add_option($lock, time(), '', false)) {
    $held = (int) get_option($lock);
    if ($held > time() - 120) {
        return new \WP_Error('opn_in_progress', __('This newsletter is already being sent.', 'omni-platform-newsletter'));
    }
    // Remove the stale lock, then acquire it again. Only one request can win.
    delete_option($lock);
    if (!add_option($lock, time(), '', false)) {
        return new \WP_Error('opn_in_progress', __('This newsletter is already being sent.', 'omni-platform-newsletter'));
    }
}
try {
    // Existing status check through the first batch. Keep the body unchanged.
} finally {
    delete_option($lock);
}
```
